title: Geriatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship
prerequisites: Intended learner: postgraduate emergency physician, emergency medicine fellow, or senior EM resident studying under the supervision of an accredited clinical programme; not a substitute for patient-care supervision.
Foundation knowledge: adult emergency assessment, acute stabilization, differential diagnosis, pharmacology, shared decision-making and transitions.
MGH describes the fellowship audience as residency-trained, ABEM-eligible/certified Emergency Physicians. This course does not establish admission eligibility.
objectives: Identify acute change in the context of baseline cognition, function and patient priorities.
Recognize serious illness and atypical presentations without anchoring on age or chronic diagnoses.
Use delirium, fall, medication, frailty and functional tools as decision supports with source-specific limits.
Integrate trauma, comorbidity, pain, cognition, mobility and goals into an evidence-aware ED plan.
Communicate safe transitions across home, facility, observation and inpatient settings.
Evaluate programme, accreditation, approval and board claims accurately; plan quality/education/research activities.

units.title: GEM scope, ageing physiology and the emergency-care lens
objectives: Distinguish physiologic ageing, multimorbidity, frailty, disability and acute illness without attributing new symptoms to age.
Use baseline function, cognition, sensory status, living context and patient priorities to shape the initial ED assessment.
Describe the difference between an individual clinical training fellowship, department accreditation and independent educational study.
topics: Reserve and atypical illness presentation; heterogeneity among adults 65+; age-friendly communication; limitations of age cut-offs; service design and professional scope.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: effect of comorbid conditions; continuum of care
ABEM general EM: undifferentiated patient, communication, systems/practice
units.casePractice: Compare a constructed older-adult presentation against a typical textbook presentation; explicitly identify which facts are unknown rather than infer them from age.
units.assessment: Short written concept map scored for accurate distinctions, baseline-first reasoning, and one explicit statement of uncertainty.

units.title: Initial assessment, baseline, function, frailty and what matters
objectives: Elicit the time course and baseline from the patient, caregiver or facility while respecting consent and communication needs.
Screen functional change, mobility, sensory barriers, nutrition, social context and frailty using a locally validated tool where appropriate.
Apply a structured geriatric assessment to ED decisions without converting screening scores into diagnoses.
topics: Baseline versus acute change; activities of daily living and instrumental ADLs; frailty concepts; hearing/vision accommodations; collateral history; the 4Ms and safety/social support.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: geriatric syndromes; continuum of care
ABEM general EM: history/exam, decision-making, communication
units.casePractice: Use the linked 2024 case report as a source-linked discussion prompt; do not copy its patient-level material into the course.
units.assessment: Observed structured oral case presentation: identify baseline, acute delta, function, supports, patient priorities and missing facts.

units.title: Atypical presentations and time-critical illness
objectives: Build a broad emergency differential for weakness, falls, functional decline, confusion, syncope and reduced intake.
Identify immediate threats and avoid premature closure when fever, pain or classic symptoms are absent.
Select tests based on presentation, pretest probability, goals and the harms/benefits of investigation.
topics: ACS/stroke and neurologic emergencies; infection/sepsis and atypical response; hypoxia, hypoglycemia, metabolic derangements, adverse drug effects; atypical trauma; diagnostic uncertainty.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: atypical presentations; intervention modifications; effect of comorbidity
ABEM general EM: medical emergencies and diagnostic reasoning
units.casePractice: Compare two fictional undifferentiated presentations and state the immediate threats that must not be missed before settling on a geriatric syndrome.
units.assessment: Timed differential-and-next-step drill scored for safety-critical threats, rationale, and avoidance of age-based anchoring.

units.title: Delirium: detect acute brain dysfunction and investigate thoughtfully
objectives: Distinguish delirium, chronic cognitive impairment and depression using acute change, fluctuation, attention and collateral history.
Select and interpret an appropriate delirium assessment tool, recognizing that negative screens do not eliminate clinical concern.
Apply 2025 GED 2.0 recommendations with their very-low-certainty qualifiers, including the uncertainty around routine head CT.
topics: Risk stratification and screening; 4AT/bCAM/CAM-ICU/mCAM/AMT-4/RASS and DTS; causes and targeted evaluation; imaging threshold; prevention/environmental care; evidence limits.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: cognitive and behavioral disorders; atypical presentations
ABEM general EM: altered mental status, neurologic/infectious/toxicologic reasoning
units.casePractice: Watch the ACEP embedded delirium recording, then use the hypothetical case in the open review to identify precipitants and missing information; do not treat its older guidance as current standard.
units.assessment: Written work-up rationale: identify acute change, immediate threats, targeted tests and how evidence uncertainty affects—not dictates—decision-making.

units.title: Dementia, behavioral symptoms, communication and safety
objectives: Recognize chronic cognitive impairment while actively searching for superimposed delirium or acute disease.
Adapt communication for hearing, vision, language and cognitive needs and involve a trusted support person with appropriate consent.
Plan a least-restrictive, cause-oriented approach to distress and agitation, with individualized medication risk/benefit review.
topics: Dementia and baseline function; delirium superimposition; behavioral distress; sensory aids, familiar people, de-escalation; safety; capacity is decision-specific and not inferred from diagnosis.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: cognitive/behavioral disorders; emergency intervention modifications; ethics
ABEM general EM: communication, altered mental status, safety
units.casePractice: Compare baseline behavior and acute change in the linked fictional simulation; make a non-pharmacologic safety plan and state escalation triggers.
units.assessment: Role-play scored on respect, clear language, sensory accommodation, collateral, safety and recognition of uncertainty.

units.title: Falls, syncope, trauma and occult injury
objectives: Treat a fall as a symptom/event requiring mechanism, precipitant, injury and recurrence assessment.
Assess high-consequence injury in older adults while accounting for anticoagulants, frailty and baseline mobility.
Use falls tools and functional/mobility assessment to create an individualized safe next step, not as a substitute for clinical judgment.
topics: Falls and near-falls; syncope/orthostasis; head injury; fragility fractures; medication/environmental risks; post-fall function; CDC STEADI tools and their outpatient context.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: trauma including falls; medication management; geriatric syndromes
ABEM general EM: trauma, syncope, neurologic and musculoskeletal emergencies
units.casePractice: Apply CDC STEADI tools as a linked follow-up resource and analyze fall/function details in the 2024 clinical case report; do not reproduce images or records.
units.assessment: Case synthesis: mechanism, injuries, precipitant differential, mobility, medication contributors and disposition support.

units.title: Medication reconciliation, polypharmacy and adverse drug events
objectives: Construct a reconciled medication list from the patient, caregiver, pharmacy, facility and records when available.
Recognize medication classes and combinations that may worsen delirium, falls, orthostasis, bleeding or renal injury.
Use the AGS Beers Criteria as a screening aid, not an automatic stop list or replacement for individualized treatment decisions.
topics: Medication discrepancies; anticholinergic/sedative burden; interactions; renal function and dose context; deprescribing discussions; Beers Criteria caveats; medication-related diagnostic mimics.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: medication management; effect of comorbidity
ABEM general EM: toxicology, pharmacology, medication reconciliation
units.casePractice: Review the linked published case report for medication-risk discussion; its accessible text does not state the de-identification process, so do not repeat case details; separately critique an entirely fictional medication list.
units.assessment: Medication audit scored for source verification, risk mechanisms, alternative causes, and not making unsupported medication changes.

units.title: Pain, agitation, wounds and intervention modification
objectives: Assess pain even when communication is impaired and consider an appropriate observational approach when needed.
Balance untreated pain, drug toxicity, sedation risk, function and the need to complete time-critical evaluation.
Modify environment and interventions for sensory, mobility, skin integrity and continence needs without asserting a single drug or dose.
topics: Pain assessment in dementia; analgesia risk-benefit; agitation and de-escalation; avoid reflexive restraint; pressure injury/wounds; mobility aids, warmth, hydration, sleep and orientation.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: emergency intervention modifications; wound care; cognitive/behavioral disorders
ABEM general EM: pain, behavioral emergencies, procedures/communication
units.casePractice: Use the fictional EMSimCases scenario to distinguish actions to maintain immediate safety from actions requiring an individualized clinical order and supervision.
units.assessment: Simulation debrief rubric: safety, humane de-escalation, reassessment, avoidable harms and evidence-based limits.

units.title: Frailty, multimorbidity and functional recovery
objectives: Explain how frailty and function modify risk and recovery without treating either as a diagnosis of irreversibility.
Integrate chronic disease, physiologic reserve, baseline mobility and patient-defined goals in emergency decisions.
Identify potential interdisciplinary supports and the limits of ED resources.
topics: Frailty concepts; vulnerability and reserve; multimorbidity; mobility/ADLs; rehab, geriatric consultation, community and facility settings; post-ED functional outcomes.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: effect of comorbid conditions; geriatric syndromes; continuum of care
ABEM general EM: disposition, risk communication
units.casePractice: Use the public case report as a reading prompt, separating its reported case facts from the learner’s proposed plan; do not infer prognosis from age alone.
units.assessment: One-page biopsychosocial formulation with explicit protective factors, functional risks and missing resources.

units.title: Palliative care, serious illness and goals-concordant decisions
objectives: Initiate a respectful conversation about what matters to the patient and clarify the role of surrogates when needed.
Distinguish palliative care from hospice and from withholding emergency stabilization.
Use shared decision-making, values, symptom burden, prognosis uncertainty and treatment burdens in care planning.
topics: Serious illness communication; decision-specific capacity; advance care planning documents; symptom relief; palliative consultation; code status is not a complete treatment plan; bias avoidance.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: ethics, palliative care and end-of-life; communication
ABEM general EM: communication, ethics, critical decisions
units.casePractice: Draft a fictional goals-of-care opening and an escalation question; do not present any script as a substitute for clinician-patient dialogue.
units.assessment: Faculty-style rubric evaluates empathy, elicitation of values, accurate distinction of palliative/hospice, and transparent uncertainty.

units.title: Disposition, transitions, safeguarding and social context
objectives: Assess whether the proposed disposition is feasible given cognition, function, support, safety and patient goals.
Deliver a clear medication, mobility, follow-up and return-precaution handoff using teach-back and appropriate receiving-team communication.
Recognize possible elder mistreatment, neglect or exploitation and follow local reporting/safeguarding processes.
topics: Home, observation, inpatient, skilled nursing and hospice contexts; caregiver availability; transportation; transitions; elder abuse; safety; handoffs; follow-up and return precautions.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: transitions; continuum of care; ethics
ABEM general EM: disposition, communication, safety
units.casePractice: Use the linked 4Ms transition review example and case report to build a fictional handoff; no patient information copied.
units.assessment: Structured discharge/handoff exercise scored for medication clarity, functional needs, safeguards, teach-back and receiving-team communication.

units.title: Geriatric ED systems, scholarship, education and quality improvement
objectives: Differentiate a fellowship approval framework, an institutional ED accreditation model and individual board certification.
Design a small local quality question using a clear population, process measure, balancing measure and equity lens.
Use evidence certainty and knowledge gaps to avoid overclaiming a pathway’s effectiveness.
topics: ACEP GEDA department accreditation; GED guidelines and implementation; QI; research appraisal; educational design; interprofessional and administration/research tracks; free learning sequence.
boardDomains: SAEM fellowship core: administration, education or research track; scholarship
ABEM general EM: practice-based learning and improvement, systems-based practice
units.casePractice: Create a fictional quality-improvement proposal and specify one intended metric plus a balancing measure; do not imply outcome efficacy from accreditation status.
units.assessment: Capstone portfolio, with rubric in assignment; identify whether each claim is programme, board, accreditation or guideline evidence.

assignment.title: Capstone: older-adult emergency care and transition plan
assignment.prompt: Using only a fictional composite case, prepare a concise assessment that states acute change/baseline, time-critical differential, targeted evaluation and its rationale, cognition/function/medication/safety factors, patient priorities and a feasible disposition/transition. Include a one-paragraph uncertainty statement and source citations. Do not use real patient information or images.

rubric.criterion: Immediate stabilization, broad differential and reasoning (25 points)
rubric.excellent: Names high-consequence threats and justifies case-specific evaluation without premature closure.
rubric.needsWork: Anchors on age, a chronic diagnosis or a single test without considering competing causes.

rubric.criterion: Baseline, cognition, communication and function (20 points)
rubric.excellent: Establishes acute delta and obtains appropriate collateral; identifies sensory/function needs and uncertainty.
rubric.needsWork: Uses a screening score or diagnosis as a substitute for baseline and assessment.

rubric.excellent: Connects mechanism/injury, functional risk, medication history and plausible harms without claiming causality.
rubric.needsWork: Omits injury/medication context or makes unsupported medication changes.

rubric.criterion: Values, team, safeguards and feasibility (15 points)
rubric.excellent: Elicits priorities, identifies supports and safeguards, considers team resources.
rubric.needsWork: Treats patient preference, age or caregiver availability as a simple proxy for capacity or safety.

rubric.excellent: States receiving setting, medication/follow-up information, mobility needs, return precautions and teach-back/handoff plan.
rubric.needsWork: Leaves a transition gap or proposes an infeasible plan.

rubric.excellent: Cites current sources and labels certainty/limits accurately.
rubric.needsWork: Overstates evidence or claims accreditation proves outcomes.

assignment.interpretation: Formative course rubric only. A course score is not validated, not a board predictor and does not represent supervised performance.

assessment.format: 10 original single-best-answer items; three short formative case tasks; capstone written transition plan; optional peer discussion using linked simulation resource.
assessment.scoringPlan: Use the assignment rubric and review each rationale. Suggested internal learning checkpoint is 80% after remediation, not an exam-passing threshold.
assessment.validityNotice: Questions are original educational items, not official or proprietary board content and have not been psychometrically validated. Scores do not predict board performance.

studyHours.type: transparent study plan (not verified course contact hours)
studyHours.note: The 60-hour learner study plan totals only viewing, reading, case/question work, capstone, and retrieval/reflection. Separately, 35.671597 hours of unique original recorded material would still need to be produced to reach the 36-hour video floor; planned clips are not ready videos and production time is not student study time.

SAEM fellowship approval and ACEP GEDA department accreditation are distinct and do not certify an individual physician.

officialProgrammes.name: MGH Emergency Medicine Geriatric Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a one-year clinical and research fellowship, with opportunity for a second year mainly focused on research and electives in education/administration; interprofessional collaboration with geriatrics, palliative care, geriatrics psychiatry and rehabilitation. It states ABEM-eligible/certified candidates and residency-trained Emergency Physicians. Public page does not publish a complete didactic lecture list or exact instructional hours. It does not state an MGH-specific ACGME accreditation status.

medical.programmeSourceScope: A distinct clinical physician fellowship, not a generic directory category or a non-physician/research-only postdoctoral supplement. Research, education and administration are scholarly tracks/options within the official fellowship description, not a separate physician specialty or separate board exam. The fellowship page reports clinical/research training and interprofessional rotations, but does not publish exact rotations, case volumes or didactic hours. SAEM provides a separate optional programme approval framework; MGH approval status was not established from the public sources checked. ACGME’s public subspecialty-program reference lists several EM fellowships but not GEM; that list does not prove an individual programme’s current accreditation status.
sourceCaveats: No existing MED-X097 programme files or lecture ledger were present; supplemental discovery contained only the original official programme-directory listing, which was preserved as the variant basis.
The MGH public fellowship page is not a complete syllabus and gives no exact didactic hours or case volumes; none are invented.
The current ABEM list checked has no GEM subspecialty certificate. MGH specifies underlying ABEM eligibility/certification.

The accessible ACGME reference omits GEM among Emergency Medicine subspecialty program types; no current individual MGH ACGME status is asserted. SAEM has its own programme approval framework; MGH approval status was not publicly confirmed.

Only the two ACEP GEDA videos with exact public Brightcove media metadata and free embedded viewing were counted. No playlist duplication, podcast/audio, short movement demonstrations, locked courses, estimates or planned recordings count.
Human clinical review has not been performed. Verify clinical content against current local protocols and authoritative guidance before any use in clinical practice.

topicGaps: The 36-hour video floor remains unmet by 35.671597 hours. Only two public specialty-focused ACEP/ GEDA clips have verified runtimes in this ledger.

Long-form specialty lecture sequences are missing for acute atypical illness, trauma/falls, medication safety, frailty/function, pain/intervention modification, palliative care, transitions, elder mistreatment and systems/QI.
GEDC case-based modules are promising but no course-specific video runtime ledger was verified, so they are not counted.

No separate public GEM board blueprint exists in the ABEM materials reviewed; this course crosswalk uses SAEM fellowship core elements and relevant general EM domains, not a fictitious GEM exam blueprint.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 79-year-old arrives with new inattention and fluctuating confusion. A family member says cognition was stable yesterday. Which first step best frames the problem?

options.text: Assume progression of dementia because of age.
Establish baseline and acute change, obtain collateral, assess immediate physiologic threats and evaluate for delirium.
Use a cognitive screen alone to diagnose dementia.
Discharge if vital signs are normal.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Acute change and fluctuation should prompt delirium assessment and evaluation for urgent causes; screening is not a diagnosis and normal vital signs do not resolve the differential.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner asks whether every older adult with suspected delirium should receive head CT. What is the best evidence-based response under the 2025 GED 2.0 guideline?

options.text: Routine CT is strongly recommended for all.
Routine CT is strongly discouraged for all.
Evidence certainty is very low; the guideline does not recommend for or against CT universally, so use case-specific clinical judgment.
CT replaces delirium screening.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 guideline found very-low-certainty evidence and no direction for or against routine head CT in older ED patients with delirium; the decision is individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: An older patient with dementia becomes acutely more restless. Which approach is safest before attributing this to baseline behavior?

options.text: Document behavioral disturbance and end evaluation.
Compare baseline with acute change, seek collateral, review medications and search for urgent causes while addressing safety and sensory needs.
Apply restraints preemptively.
Assume urinary infection without assessment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Dementia can coexist with delirium; acute change requires cause-oriented assessment, collateral and humane safety-focused care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient reports a fall but has no obvious injury. Which plan best reflects a geriatric ED approach?

options.text: Treat the fall solely as a mechanical event and omit function.
Assess mechanism, injuries, potential precipitant, medication context, baseline/current mobility and safe supports.
Use TUG alone to clear the patient.
Assume the fall is benign if the patient denies pain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A fall can reflect injury, syncope, illness, medications or functional decline; assessment must consider injury, cause and functional safety. STEADI tools are aids, not a stand-alone ED clearance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A medication list includes a first-generation antihistamine and benzodiazepine in a patient with falls and confusion. What is the best interpretation of Beers Criteria?

options.text: Both drugs are absolutely contraindicated in every older adult.
They are potential medication risks worth reviewing in clinical context; the criteria support rather than replace individualized/shared decisions.
The list proves the medication caused delirium.
Stop all listed medicines without reconciliation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Beers flags potentially inappropriate drugs and relevant risks but should be applied thoughtfully; it does not prove causality or mandate unilateral discontinuation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with dementia is being assessed for pain but has difficulty describing it. Which statement is best?

options.text: Pain cannot be present without a reliable verbal report.
Use an appropriate observational assessment and clinical context, reassess response, and balance pain and medication harms.
Avoid analgesia because it may cause delirium.
Give a sedative instead of assessing pain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pain assessment should adapt to communication limits; both untreated pain and medication adverse effects matter, and treatment is individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: A decision-maker describes a preference to return home, but the patient now needs help ambulating and the caregiver is unavailable overnight. Which disposition reasoning is best?

options.text: Discharge because preference alone determines feasibility.
Integrate what matters, medication, mentation, mobility, safety/support, available care setting and follow-up; explain trade-offs and reassess options.
Admit every person over 65.
Use age as a proxy for capacity.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Geriatric transition planning requires values, function, supports and setting; neither age nor one screening factor alone determines disposition.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellowship directory lists a Geriatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship, and a learner asks which separate GEM board examination follows it. What is accurate?

options.text: ABEM has a geriatric emergency medicine subspecialty exam.
The 2026 ABEM subspecialty list does not include GEM; underlying EM ABEM eligibility/certification is relevant to the MGH fellowship, but no separate GEM board exam is listed.
SAEM course completion grants ABEM certification.
GEDA accreditation certifies an individual physician.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The MGH page describes ABEM-eligible/certified emergency physicians; ABEM’s subspecialty list contains no GEM certification. SAEM approval and ACEP ED accreditation are different from individual board certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: A colleague says the clinical case report linked in this curriculum can be copied into slides because it is freely viewable. What is correct?

options.text: Free viewing grants unlimited reuse.
Link to the publicly viewable case; its source copyright remains, and no patient material/images should be copied or rehosted absent permission.
Remove the author names and copy all images.
A published case is public domain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free access is not a rehosting license. This course links to the case and explicitly does not reproduce its patient narrative or images.

practiceQuestions.stem: A local GED quality proposal claims accreditation itself proves reduced mortality. What is the strongest critique?

options.text: Accreditation status alone establishes causal clinical benefit.
Define the population, intervention/process, outcome and balancing measures; evaluate evidence and confounding rather than infer causality from accreditation.
Only patient satisfaction should be measured.
No quality measure is needed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guidelines and accreditation can guide structure/process, but an outcome claim needs an appropriate evaluation and cannot be inferred from designation alone.

title: Emergency Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship; institutional listing is an EM/CCM-labelled Internal Medicine-based Critical Care Medicine track, not evidence of a standalone EM-CCM board or independently verified ACGME accreditation.-aligned independent study

prerequisites.level: Postgraduate physician self-study for emergency medicine or other physician trainees; advanced specialty learning, not entry-level medical education.
prerequisites.recommended: Medical degree and prior grounding in physiology, pharmacology, emergency/acute care, ECG/ABG interpretation and basic critical care; supervised clinical training is required for clinical application.
prerequisites.notRequiredToEnroll: This independent online curriculum does not verify credentials, admit fellows or confer training credit.

objectives: Synthesize stabilization, airway/respiratory support and ED-to-ICU transitions under uncertainty.
Reason across shock phenotypes, sepsis, cardiopulmonary, neurologic, renal, metabolic, toxicologic and multisystem critical illness.

Explain principles, risks and limits of common ICU procedures, devices and ultrasound while recognizing that knowledge is not procedural competence.
Communicate whole-patient goals, reassessment, interprofessional coordination, ICU liberation and post-ICU needs.
Recognize the distinction between programme listing, ACGME accreditation, board route, board examination, licensure and practice competence.

mapping.institution: Brigham and Women’s Hospital / Mass General Brigham
mapping.name: BWH Emergency Medicine Critical Care Medicine Fellowship – IM Specialization (official page heading: “Emergency Critical Care Medicine Fellowship – IM Specialization”)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page calls this an Internal Medicine-based critical care training program, identifies it as the BWH EM/CCM Fellowship, describes collaboration with Anesthesia and Surgery and lists medical/nonmedical ICU and selectives. It describes 24 months of clinical training, ≥16 months meaningful direct patient care, ≥12 months CCM, including 6 months medical and 6 months non-medical ICU, and ≤12 required ICU months. Published rotation list: BWH MICU 12 weeks, VA MICU 2, South Shore ICU 24; BWH surgical ICU 4, thoracic ICU 6, cardiac surgery ICU 4, MGH Blake 12 liver transplant ICU 2; listed selectives include ECMO, neuro/neurosurgical ICU, echo, infectious diseases, nutrition, renal, transplant, ultrasound, transport and research. These numbers/rotations are the institutional webpage’s description, not independently audited schedule or case volume. ACGME accreditation for this exact listing was not independently confirmed.

topicGaps: All topics lack verified counted free lecture videos in this session because direct public media runtime/access verification failed; every candidate video remains excluded.
The 2025 AHA guidelines page is accessible, but public video lecture runtimes/access were not verified; login-only instructor content is excluded.

MGB page is public programme description; exact ACGME status, full institutional syllabus, exact case volume, and board pathway approval for this exact programme were not verified.

The complete target is represented by 24 planned 90-minute source-backed sessions (36 planned hours), but none is recorded, rendered, uploaded or verified; the actual verified-hour gap remains 36 hours.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship; institutional listing is an EM/CCM-labelled Internal Medicine-based Critical Care Medicine track, not evidence of a standalone EM-CCM board or independently verified ACGME accreditation.
boardNames: ABIM Critical Care Medicine (jointly developed/administered with ABEM for the EM–IM CCM route)
ABEM Emergency Medicine primary certification (prerequisite/parallel credential, not a separate EM-CCM board)
American Board of Surgery Surgical Critical Care (separate pathway after qualifying training)
American Board of Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine (separate pathway after qualifying training)
United Council for Neurologic Subspecialties Neurocritical Care (separate discipline/pathway)
ABEM/ABIM Internal Medicine–Emergency Medicine–Critical Care Medicine triple certification (separate six-year integrated route)
medical.boardStatus: No separate “Emergency Critical Care Medicine” specialty board exam was identified. Emergency physicians may pursue distinct board pathways in critical care through ABIM/ABEM (IM-CCM), ABA/ABEM (ACCM), ABS/ABEM (Surgical Critical Care), or UCNS neurocritical care; the joint ABEM/ABIM triple board is a separate six-year integrated training route. The institution’s page does not establish any learner’s board eligibility or the specific pathway approved for this MGB track.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Board eligibility is controlled by the relevant board and accredited training pathway. The institutional course listing is not proof of ACGME accreditation or a board-eligible pathway. ABEM states that it credentials eligible emergency physicians for the ABIM-developed/administered IM-CCM exam. Verify current policies directly; no eligibility, certification or exam outcome is promised.

officialProgrammes.institution: Brigham and Women’s Hospital / Mass General Brigham
officialProgrammes.name: BWH Emergency Medicine Critical Care Medicine Fellowship – IM Specialization (official page heading: “Emergency Critical Care Medicine Fellowship – IM Specialization”)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page calls this an Internal Medicine-based critical care training program, identifies it as the BWH EM/CCM Fellowship, describes collaboration with Anesthesia and Surgery and lists medical/nonmedical ICU and selectives. It describes 24 months of clinical training, ≥16 months meaningful direct patient care, ≥12 months CCM, including 6 months medical and 6 months non-medical ICU, and ≤12 required ICU months. Published rotation list: BWH MICU 12 weeks, VA MICU 2, South Shore ICU 24; BWH surgical ICU 4, thoracic ICU 6, cardiac surgery ICU 4, MGH Blake 12 liver transplant ICU 2; listed selectives include ECMO, neuro/neurosurgical ICU, echo, infectious diseases, nutrition, renal, transplant, ultrasound, transport and research. These numbers/rotations are the institutional webpage’s description, not independently audited schedule or case volume. ACGME accreditation for this exact listing was not independently confirmed.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is the single exact institutional variant carried forward from the supplied packet. MGB official page establishes the institution-listed clinical fellowship opportunity and its stated IM-based programme characterization. No additional Harvard-affiliated or Johns Hopkins variant was verified in this scoped task; generic directory categories and separate ABS/ABA/UCNS pathways are not conflated with the MGB track. No claim is made that it is research-only or non-physician; the official page is clearly physician GME and describes clinical ICU rotations plus research/selective options.
sourceCaveats: Human clinical review has not been performed.
MGB official page distinctly identifies an IM-based CCM programme despite EM/CCM fellowship naming; accreditation status for this exact listing was not independently verified.
Institutional rotation descriptions are not board certification requirements, ACGME verification, proof of case volumes, or guarantee of applicant eligibility.
ABEM/ABIM, ABA/ABEM, ABS/ABEM and UCNS routes are distinct. Do not call them one exam or infer a universal separate EM-CCM examination.

Clinical recommendations evolve: SCCM sepsis source is 2021; PADIS core guideline 2018 with a linked 2025 focused update; AHA CPR/ECC is 2025; ATS ARDS update 2024; KDIGO 2026 AKI/AKD update remains draft per current page.
No completed/rendered original lecture clips; the complete pilot script is an original educational script, not medical advice or operational clinical instruction.

This independent educational course grants no Harvard/MGB/Johns Hopkins affiliation, accreditation, clinical training, licensure, board eligibility, procedure competence or certification. It cannot guarantee examination success.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional adult with suspected infection, an elevated lactate is found. Which interpretation is most defensible?

options.text: It alone establishes sepsis.
It alone excludes sepsis if normal.
It is an adjunct that modifies probability and should be interpreted with the full clinical picture.
It proves tissue hypoxia as the only cause.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SSC suggests lactate measurement in suspected sepsis, but lactate alone is neither sufficiently sensitive nor specific to rule in or out sepsis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with sepsis-induced hypoperfusion is being resuscitated. Which approach best reflects the 2021 SSC recommendation language?

options.text: Give no fluid unless static filling pressures are low.
Consider at least 30 mL/kg crystalloid in the first 3 h, then reassess using dynamic measures and patient context.
Give starch as first-line fluid.
Use lactate normalization as the only resuscitation endpoint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2021 recommendation suggests at least 30 mL/kg crystalloid within 3 hours for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion/shock and suggests dynamic measures; recommendations require individual reassessment and are not a universal automatic protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: For an adult with ARDS receiving invasive ventilation, which target is consistent with ATS guidance?

options.text: Tidal volume 10–12 mL/kg actual body weight.
Tidal volume 4–8 mL/kg predicted body weight and plateau pressure below 30 cm H2O.
Routine HFOV for moderate/severe ARDS.
Avoid prone positioning in severe ARDS.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ATS recommends limiting tidal volume to 4–8 mL/kg predicted body weight and plateau pressure <30 cm H2O; prone positioning >12 hours/day is recommended for severe ARDS, and routine HFOV is discouraged.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult has acute bilateral pulmonary arterial thrombi with sustained hypotension and shock. Which hemodynamic descriptor most distinguishes “massive” PE in the linked ATS case framing?

options.text: Hypoxemia alone.
Concurrent DVT.
Hemodynamic compromise/shock.
Pulmonary hypertension alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ATS case describes massive PE by hemodynamic compromise; this is an older case and terminology/management should be interpreted with current PE guidance, not as a treatment protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: A critically ill patient has new AKI and the learner proposes using an old KDIGO recommendation as if no update is pending. What is the best next step?

options.text: Treat the 2012 guideline as current indefinitely.
Recognize a 2026 update draft is under development; distinguish draft proposals from published guidance and verify the current standard.
Use the draft as final.
Ignore kidney-replacement therapy evidence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: KDIGO now identifies a 2026 AKI/AKD guideline draft as under development; the linked 2012 guideline remains the published guideline on that page pending final publication.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a learner considering an EM-to-critical-care pathway, what does the official ABEM page say about the IM-CCM examination?

options.text: ABEM alone creates an EM-CCM examination.
ABEM credentials eligible emergency physicians and ABIM develops/administers the joint IM-CCM exam.
There is no exam.
A course certificate is equivalent to board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABEM identifies its role in credentialing EM candidates while ABIM develops/administers the IM-CCM subspecialty exam. Eligibility depends on prescribed training and other requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the ACGME length stated in its 2025 Critical Care Medicine requirements for a standard CCM program?

options.text: 6 months.
12 months for everyone.
24 months, with a 12-month option for fellows with a qualifying prior internal-medicine subspecialty program.
36 months for all EM entrants.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 ACGME CCM requirements state 24 months, with a 12-month possibility for specified fellows completing a qualifying prior subspecialty fellowship; this is an accreditation requirement, not a guarantee about any individual route.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about Radiopaedia case images is safest for a free self-study course?

options.text: Free viewing grants unrestricted redistribution.
Copy all figures into a course without attribution.
Link to the case; if using images, honor attribution and CC BY-NC-SA and confirm noncommercial/course-use limits before reuse.
Remove attribution to anonymize.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Radiopaedia describes CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and explicit commercial/course restrictions; links are safer than copying, and free-to-view is not blanket rehost permission.

practiceQuestions.stem: In an ICU patient whose agitation is being treated, which is an appropriate evidence-use statement?

options.text: Sedation replaces pain assessment and delirium evaluation.
Use a structured patient-centered assessment framework, acknowledging PADIS 2018 and reviewing the linked 2025 focused update for currency.
One sedative is mandatory for every patient.
Deep sedation is always preferred.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SCCM PADIS organizes pain, sedation/agitation, delirium, immobility and sleep; a 2025 focused update exists, so learners should check version-specific guidance rather than overgeneralize.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 2025 AHA guideline page includes public recommendations and a login-only instructor update. Which content may this curriculum count as a free lecture video?

options.text: Any course requiring instructor login.
A publicly reachable, observed-duration video after access and runtime verification.
An unrendered clip plan.
A paid course listed on the page.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Only actual free recordings with verified public access and observed duration count; a guideline webpage, login content and planned video are not lecture hours.

assignment.title: Educator capstone portfolio: design and evaluate one EM teaching intervention
assignment.description: Select a bounded learner-education problem (not a real patient care incident). Build a needs assessment, objectives-to-assessment map, lesson plan, one original formative assessment, feedback/observation plan, evaluation logic model, accessibility and rights checklist, and a revision memo. Deliver an original 6-10 minute script or storyboard; no patient data, clinical video, or protected materials.
deliverables: Problem statement and stakeholder map
Measurable objectives and curriculum map
Teaching plan and fictional educational case
Original assessment items/rubric and feedback method
Evaluation plan with measures and limitations
Privacy/accessibility/licensing checklist
6-10 minute source-cited pilot script
Peer-review response and revision memo

rubric.excellent: Problem is bounded; stakeholders/context are considered; objectives, teaching, and assessment align.
rubric.developing: Some components align but the needs basis or objective measurability is unclear.
rubric.insufficient: Activity-first plan with no defensible need or assessable outcomes.

rubric.excellent: Technique matches learner/context; active participation, accessibility, and psychological safety are planned.
rubric.developing: Technique is plausible but adaptation or inclusion plan is incomplete.
rubric.insufficient: One-size-fits-all lecture or no learner-engagement plan.

rubric.excellent: Assessment is objective-linked; observation/feedback is behavior-specific; limits are stated.
rubric.developing: Assessment exists but validity or feedback plan is weak.
rubric.insufficient: Claims competence from attendance, a single score, or an unstructured impression.

rubric.excellent: Indicators match a logic model; methods and inference limits are explicit.
rubric.developing: Evaluation is proposed but causal or measurement assumptions remain vague.
rubric.insufficient: Uses satisfaction alone as proof of learning or outcomes.

rubric.excellent: No patient media/PHI; permission and licenses are tracked; accessibility is addressed.
rubric.developing: Risks are identified but safeguards lack detail.
rubric.insufficient: Uses patient records/media or copyrighted materials without authorization.

rubric.excellent: Authoritative sources support claims and current institutional/board rules are not conflated.
rubric.developing: Some relevant sources but claims are weakly mapped.
rubric.insufficient: Invents accreditation/credential claims or relies on sources without support.

rubric.excellent: Peer feedback is responded to with justified substantive revision and acknowledged limitations.
rubric.developing: Reflection is present but revision is mostly cosmetic.

assignment.passingRule: For self-study only: target >=80/100, with no critical privacy/rights/clinical-scope breach; not a validated credential or predictor. Rework any unsafe item irrespective of score.

assessment.limitations: Not psychometrically validated, not official board material, and not a substitute for a formal MHPE degree, fellowship, accredited GME, clinical supervision, or board examination.

topicGaps: No counted free, runtime-verified external lecture video corpus was established in this pass. Publicly listed candidate videos had blocked/failed duration/playback checks.
All 12 units need future original lecture production or independently runtime-verified open recordings; the plan contains 72 planned 30-minute recording modules (36 hours), not finished media.
No ABEM medical-education exam blueprint exists; assessment maps to educator practice frameworks rather than clinical EM board knowledge.
No public detailed MGB fellowship didactic schedule, recordings, or full institutional course content was identified.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.family: Acute, emergency, pulmonary and critical care
medical.trackType: Supplementary clinical physician fellowship (academic medical-education training; not a distinct board specialty)
boardNames: American Board of Emergency Medicine (ABEM) — Emergency Medicine certification is the relevant prerequisite context; no separate medical-education fellowship board exam/certification identified.
medical.boardStatus: ABEM lists EM subspecialty certifications and focused-practice designations; medical education is not listed as a separate ABEM subspecialty or exam. This is an academic physician-educator fellowship, not an EM clinical board-review track. The official MGB page states applicants should be ABEM board-eligible or board-certified. A separate clinical board exam does not exist for this medical-education fellowship based on the current ABEM list checked 2026-10-07.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: MGB programme entry is separate from ABEM eligibility. MGB page: applicants should be ABEM board eligible or board certified and able to practice clinical EM in Massachusetts if selected. ABEM eligibility is determined by ABEM after required accredited/approved EM training and medical-licensure criteria; this self-study course confers none of those statuses. Verify current policies with ABEM and MGB.

officialProgrammes.institution: Mass General Brigham (Harvard-affiliated academic health system)
officialProgrammes.name: Fellowship in Emergency Medicine Medical Education (official page calls it the Harvard-Affiliated Emergency Medicine Medical Education Fellowship)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a two-year fellowship with exposure at MGH and BWH; required core includes MGH Institute MS in Health Professions Education, GME administration mentorship, biweekly fellowship-director mentorship, annual CORD meeting, SAEM ARMED MedEd, portfolio development, education research, and CCC/administrative exposure. CORD MERC and ACEP Teaching Fellowship are listed as optional. Public page does not disclose full lecture sequence or exact didactic hours.

medical.programmeSourceScope: One actual institutional physician-focused academic fellowship, not a generic directory category or a research-only postdoctoral listing. MGB and its Harvard-affiliated EM group describe the programme as instructional-design and education-research training for physician educators and leadership. It is a two-year joint exposure at MGH and BWH, not two separately verified programmes. It includes teaching, programme administration, and supervised education research. It is not itself established here as ACGME-accredited and is not a clinical EM specialty or a combined residency. Harvard Medical School lists both MGH and BWH among its affiliates.
sourceCaveats: MGB official page was fetched directly. It supports the stated programme scope, duration, components, application criterion, and MGH/BWH exposure; it does not publish all proprietary lecture content or exact didactic hours.
ABEM current list was checked directly; no medical-education subspecialty certification or separate exam is listed. The statement is based on current public listings, not a legal determination.

ACGME EM public requirements page supplies EM accreditation framework, but no conclusion of programme accreditation or non-accreditation is made for this MGB academic fellowship; status is not stated on the fellowship page and not independently confirmed in the public ACGME finder.
SAEM Teaching on Shift PDF is freely linked and fetched, but reuse license was not identified; course links to it only and does not republish its content.
SAEM ARMED MedEd is an application-based paid cohort course (page published current tuition); ACEP Teaching Fellowship is conference-based/paid. Neither is counted as a free lecture source.

Runtime collection: public Colorado playlist returned 9 item IDs/titles via flat public metadata, but watch-page runtime probes failed with HTTP 429/403. A COMSEP directory describes a 17-minute outbound teaching video; Vimeo interstitial prevented playback verification. No bypass or login was attempted, so these are uncounted.

No patient records, clinical images, or protected clips were copied. EM Sim Cases states CC BY-SA 4.0; CPC-EM journal index states CC BY 4.0, but article-level patient privacy and third-party figure rights must be checked before reuse.
Original clip scripts/plans remain planned and have no recordings, renderings, duration probes, URLs, or free-access status. No original content is represented as a ready video.

No human clinical review performed. This independent educational resource creates no institutional affiliation, accredited training, licensure, ABEM eligibility, board certification, procedure competence, or guarantee of passing.
The public MGB application page lists an August 28, 2026 application deadline; this date had passed on dateChecked. Applicants should verify the next cycle directly.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A faculty educator wants learners to “understand feedback.” Which revision most directly makes the objective observable?

options.text: Learners will appreciate the value of feedback.
Learners will describe one observed behavior, its effect, and one agreed next step in a role-play feedback exchange.
Learners will attend a feedback lecture.
Learners will become better educators.

practiceQuestions.rationale: B specifies assessable learner behavior in context. The other choices are attitudinal, attendance-based, or too broad to assess.

practiceQuestions.stem: A new learner presents a case and gives a broad differential. In a brief on-shift teaching moment, which move best supports reasoning while keeping the learner active?

options.text: Immediately provide a long list of diagnoses without asking how the learner reasoned.
Ask the learner to commit to a leading possibility and explain the evidence, then add one transferable teaching point.
Use an exhaustive written examination while active care is underway.
End the encounter without feedback because shift teaching must be long.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A structured brief method can elicit commitment and reasoning before a concise teaching point; the educational technique must not delay care or privacy safeguards.

practiceQuestions.stem: An educator observes one successful simulation performance and wants to document a learner as independently competent across all settings. What is the strongest response?

options.text: One successful observation proves competence across contexts.
Aggregate multiple observations and other evidence across contexts, make intended-use limits explicit, and follow the program’s authorized assessment process.
Avoid documenting any observation.
Convert the observation directly to a board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Competence judgments require appropriate evidence and context. A single observation is limited; independent certification cannot result from a local educational score.

practiceQuestions.stem: A program is revising a curriculum after learners report poor confidence. What should an educator do before choosing a lecture as the solution?

options.text: Treat low confidence as proof of missing knowledge.
Conduct a needs assessment across learners, tasks, and system context; identify outcomes and constraints before choosing instruction.
Copy a neighboring program’s curriculum.
Choose the longest available video.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Needs assessment is a planning step; confidence alone does not establish the source of a performance problem. Context and stakeholders matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best characterizes the ACGME Clinician Educator Milestones?

options.text: They are a required accreditation checklist for all faculty.
They are a developmental framework for assessing and supporting clinician educators, and are explicitly not an ACGME accreditation requirement.
They confer a medical specialty board certificate.
They replace clinical specialty Milestones.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME states that the Clinician Educator Milestones support educator development and are not an accreditation requirement. They do not create board status.
practiceQuestions.domain: Clinician educator framework and accreditation literacy

practiceQuestions.stem: A researcher is studying how residents experience feedback after night shifts. Which design is most directly aligned with the question as phrased?

options.text: A randomized drug trial.
Qualitative interviews with an appropriate sampling and reflexivity plan, with ethics/privacy review as required.
A board examination score alone.
A satisfaction survey assumed to prove learning.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The question concerns experiences and meaning, making qualitative interviews a plausible fit. Design must still address selection, ethics, and analytic rigor; no single method is mandated.

practiceQuestions.stem: A faculty member wants to assess whether a teaching intervention improved curriculum performance. Which conclusion is defensible from a pre/post score increase alone?

options.text: The intervention caused all observed gains.
Scores changed after implementation, but alternative explanations and measurement properties must be considered before causal claims.
The assessment is valid for every use.
Learners are competent for unsupervised practice.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A simple pre/post comparison is vulnerable to confounding, maturation, testing effects, and measurement issues; the observed change is not alone causal or a competence warrant.

practiceQuestions.stem: An emergency department teaching video includes a visible patient monitor with name and date of birth. What should the educator do before using it in a public course?

options.text: Upload it because educational intent automatically authorizes disclosure.
Do not publish as-is; remove or replace protected information, obtain required permissions/consents, and verify all media rights and institutional policies.
Blur only the patient’s face and assume all rights are cleared.
Ask learners not to share it.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Educational purpose is not blanket permission to disclose patient information or reuse copyrighted media. De-identification, consent, institutional rules, and rights must be evaluated.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellowship page states that fellows attend a master’s program, conduct supervised education research, teach, and participate in program administration. Which inference is justified?

options.text: The fellowship itself is an ACGME-accredited residency and grants board eligibility.
The programme is a physician-focused educational fellowship with described research, teaching, and administrative components; accreditation and separate board status must be verified independently.
Its two years establish eligibility for an education board exam.
Its curriculum equals all proprietary institutional lectures.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The institutional page describes these components and eligibility for the fellowship; that does not establish ACGME accreditation or a distinct board credential.

practiceQuestions.stem: A CCC reviews a learner’s portfolio. Which practice best reduces the risk that a single salient event dominates the judgment?

options.text: Rely on the most recent narrative only.
Triangulate longitudinal observations, assessment methods, contexts, and narrative evidence; examine bias and document uncertainty.
Ignore narrative evidence.
Make decisions based on a single unstructured impression.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Longitudinal programmatic evidence and explicit attention to context and bias are more defensible than a single impression; local policies govern official progression decisions.

title: Global Emergency Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (institutional fellowship in a clinical field; not a distinct board specialty in reviewed ABEM certification sources)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: MD/DO or comparable physician background and completed Emergency Medicine residency-level training assumed; this is an educational prerequisite, not a verified entry rule for every jurisdiction.
Current general emergency-medicine clinical knowledge and competence; learner must use current local clinical guidance and work only within their own licensed/supervised scope.
Working knowledge of epidemiology, study design, biostatistics, program evaluation and basic humanitarian terminology is helpful; introductory refreshers are provided.
English reading proficiency for the linked materials; translations may exist but have not been audited.
objectives: Analyze an emergency-care pathway from scene/first contact through transport, emergency unit, referral and early inpatient care, while identifying context-specific system gaps.

Apply a structured evidence-based approach to acute illness/injury cases at the level of a previously trained emergency physician, including uncertainty, reassessment, handover and limits of setting-specific guidance.
Plan humanitarian and disaster response in coordination with affected-country authorities and established EMT/health cluster frameworks.
Design reciprocal, ethical, feasible research or a programme-evaluation plan with local partners, appropriate data governance, measurable outcomes and transparent limits.

Communicate across language/cultural contexts, support education and leadership, and distinguish educational participation from licensure, credentialing, deployment readiness or procedural competence.
Map general ABEM EM cognitive domains to applicable foundational cases without implying a separate Global EM board exam or passing prediction.

units.title: Global EM as a field: clinical practice, systems and roles
objectives: Distinguish global EM from a separate medical specialty, institutional fellowship, and global-health supplement.
Map the BWH programme’s six training areas without presenting them as a public rotation schedule.
Explain why cross-context learning requires local partnership and scope-of-practice awareness.
topics: Definitions and scope; systems-building; reciprocal partnership; local leadership; limits of short-term visits.
boardDomains: Clinical practice/medical knowledge (general EM foundation); ABEM EM Model is not a Global EM exam blueprint.
units.casePractice: Compare two public programme descriptions and classify each statement as an institutional programme fact, board rule, or general field concept.
units.assessment: Short written taxonomy; rubric: evidence accuracy 40%, distinctions 30%, careful qualification 30%.

units.title: Emergency-care systems and needs assessment
objectives: Trace urgent care from community/scene through transport, ED, and early inpatient care.
Use a framework to identify service gaps and context-specific priorities without importing assumptions from a high-resource system.
Specify a small set of measurable process and outcome indicators with denominators.
topics: WHO ECSF; access and first contact; referral; workforce/coordination; systems assessment; indicators and data quality.
boardDomains: ABEM systems-based practice/clinical decision making, general EM; WHO system functions are not board exam weights.
units.casePractice: Build a fictional district-level service map and rank three bottlenecks; label each indicator numerator, denominator, and data limitations.
units.assessment: Systems map + 500-word memo; rubric: completeness 25%, contextual fit 25%, indicator validity 25%, feasibility/equity 25%.

units.title: First-contact acute care in resource-constrained settings
objectives: Apply a structured ABCDE/SAMPLE reasoning sequence to a fictional undifferentiated patient.
Identify immediate instability, reassessment triggers, and escalation/transfer needs using locally available capability.
Explain where a first-contact care manual is useful and where it is not a substitute for local protocols or supervision.
topics: WHO/ICRC BEC; difficulty breathing, shock, altered mental status, injury; life-course considerations; handover.
boardDomains: General EM patient-care competencies; ABEM EM Model; BEC is cross-cadre open training, not specialist fellowship certification.
units.casePractice: Structured oral case using an instructor-authored fictional vignette; learner must state safety checks, next information sought, reassessment and transfer contingencies.
units.assessment: Case performance rubric: prioritization 30%, reasoning 25%, reassessment 20%, communication 15%, limits/localization 10%.

units.title: Prehospital care, triage, referral and continuity
objectives: Describe how ambulance/dispatch, first responders, receiving facilities, and referral networks interact.
Choose and defend a triage approach only after specifying setting, objective, and governing protocol.
Communicate a structured handover and plan for referral failure.
topics: Access, triage, prehospital pathways, transport barriers, referral, handoff, crowding and continuity.
boardDomains: General EM prioritization, reassessment and communication; ABEM case types are not a global system blueprint.
units.casePractice: Use an anonymized published/linked case only if rights permit; otherwise use fictional patient and a fictional regional referral map. Produce a handover and process map.
units.assessment: Handover rubric: key risks 25%, concise structure 25%, referral contingency 25%, dignity/language 15%, source limits 10%.

units.title: Humanitarian response, disaster and EMT operations
objectives: Explain EMT classification and the affected state’s authority in accepting, registering, licensing, tasking and coordinating external teams.
Integrate clinical capacity with logistics, self-sufficiency, referral, information management and safe exit/hand-over.
Distinguish clinical surge care from disaster management and humanitarian coordination functions.
topics: All-hazards response; WHO EMT initiative; local authority and coordination; team capability/registration; disaster risk; surge and safe exit.
boardDomains: Emergency practice in mass casualty/disaster; ABEM prioritization and systems-based practice, not a distinct GEM board domain.
units.casePractice: Fictional tabletop scenario: prepare a one-page team offer-of-assistance and registration checklist; do not deploy or claim operational authorization.
units.assessment: Tabletop rubric: needs alignment 25%, coordination/authority 25%, clinical safety/logistics 25%, transition/exit 15%, evidence 10%.

units.title: Humanitarian law, ethics, protection and conflict health
objectives: Identify how impartiality, neutrality, humanity and independence differ from clinical duty and local legal obligations.
Recognize duty-of-care, security, protection and ethical dilemmas; refer decisions to competent local and organizational leadership.
Explain that medical neutrality and facility/worker protection are operational and legal commitments, not an immunity guarantee.
topics: International humanitarian law; health care in danger; human rights; safeguarding, consent, confidentiality, staff safety and humanitarian principles.
boardDomains: Professionalism/communication and safety (general EM); no separate board test.
units.casePractice: Analyze a fictional conflict-health dilemma with a rights/risks/authority matrix and a stop-work/escalation option.
units.assessment: Ethics memo rubric: identify stakeholders 25%, norms/uncertainty 25%, safety and escalation 25%, non-extractive reasoning 25%.

units.title: Refugee health, displacement and cross-cultural practice
objectives: Describe how displacement, language, legal status, trauma and access barriers affect emergency care.
Use an interpreter-centered, trauma-informed encounter without stereotyping a population.
Plan referral and continuity around privacy and realistic service availability.
topics: Refugee/displacement health; culturally responsive communication; interpreter use; gender and disability inclusion; privacy; access and continuity.
boardDomains: General EM communication/patient care, population/context; no Global EM blueprint.
units.casePractice: Fictional standardized-patient encounter with interpreter role; identify structural barriers and a non-coercive follow-up plan.
units.assessment: Encounter rubric: respectful communication 30%, safety 25%, cultural humility 20%, privacy 15%, feasible plan 10%.

units.title: Global public health, outbreaks and emergency surveillance
objectives: Differentiate surveillance signals, outbreak investigation, and clinical diagnosis.
Frame a descriptive epidemiology question and select a suitable numerator, denominator, time, place and person variables.
Explain when local public health notification and current guidance take precedence over generic teaching content.
topics: Outbreak readiness; surveillance; line list; case definitions; epidemic curves; infection prevention; risk communication; One Health/climate considerations.
boardDomains: General EM infectious disease/patient care; epidemiologic methods are program learning goals, not ABEM-weighted GEM domains.
units.casePractice: Use a fabricated dataset explicitly labelled synthetic to create a line list and descriptive plot; do not enter patient data.
units.assessment: Epidemiology assignment rubric: question/design 20%, calculations 30%, bias/limitations 25%, ethics/communication 25%.

units.title: Global EM research, implementation science and grant design
objectives: Construct a feasible, locally meaningful research question and distinguish implementation evaluation from efficacy research.
Select quantitative/qualitative methods and prespecify sampling, outcomes, bias, missingness and analysis.
Identify when ethics review, local permissions, data governance and community engagement are required; never collect real patient data in this course.
topics: Research design; measurement; biostatistics; implementation/program evaluation; co-authorship; local leadership; grant logic model.
boardDomains: ABEM general EM medical knowledge does not define research certification; programme expects publishable research as described by BWH source.
units.casePractice: Draft an IRB/ethics planning memo for a hypothetical minimal-risk service evaluation; do not represent it as approved research.
units.assessment: Protocol rubric: question 20%, method 25%, ethics/data 30%, partnership 15%, feasibility 10%.

units.title: Programme design, funding, monitoring and sustainability
objectives: Write a causal pathway from local need to activities, outputs, outcomes and assumptions.
Select indicators that avoid overclaiming attribution and include equity, acceptability, service quality and sustainability.
Build an implementation/exit plan that transfers ownership and avoids dependence.
topics: Logic models; stakeholder map; budget assumptions; monitoring and evaluation; health policy; localization; sustainability and exit.
boardDomains: Programme leadership and systems-based practice; no specialty board exam.
units.casePractice: Create a one-page proposal for a fictional emergency-care-system strengthening project; include counterfactual/limitations and handover to local partners.
units.assessment: Proposal rubric: problem/partner fit 20%, theory of change 20%, indicators 20%, budget/sustainability 20%, equity/ethics 20%.

units.title: Teaching, leadership and bidirectional capacity strengthening
objectives: Set learning outcomes for a learner group and context using an appropriate teaching method.
Use debrief/feedback methods that avoid deficit narratives and support learner agency.
Plan mentorship and capacity strengthening with locally identified goals and evaluation.
topics: Adult learning; instructor development; mentoring; leadership; supervision; bidirectional learning; evaluation of educational programs.
boardDomains: General EM communication/professionalism; BWH training description includes education/teaching responsibilities but public rotation details are limited.
units.casePractice: Develop a 20-minute teach-back with objectives, accessible handout outline and a pre/post evaluation item; use no copied protected slides.
units.assessment: Teaching rubric: alignment 25%, learner/context fit 25%, engagement/debrief 20%, assessment 20%, attribution/accessibility 10%.

units.title: Clinical integration, board cognition and professional limits
objectives: Apply general EM reasoning to undifferentiated cases while articulating uncertainty and reassessment.
Use ABEM’s published general exam framing without falsely claiming a global EM exam or passing predictor.
Distinguish educational observation from supervised competence, privileges, licensure and deployment readiness.
topics: Clinical decision-making; communication; prioritization; reassessment; procedure/ultrasound boundaries; readiness/credentialing; transfer to general EM standards.
boardDomains: ABEM EM Model 2022 and Certifying Exam public domains; no GME fellowship board-domain weights are published in reviewed sources.
units.casePractice: Write a short oral-board-style explanation for fictional case, including uncertainty, a safe disposition/transfer and what must be checked in current local guidance.
units.assessment: Oral defense rubric: differential/prioritization 25%, evidence/update 25%, communication 20%, reassessment/disposition 20%, limitations 10%.

assignment.title: Capstone: locally led emergency-care-system improvement concept
deliverables: A 1,500–2,000 word needs and pathway assessment using a public WHO/IFEM framework and sources; clearly mark known facts versus assumptions.
A 1-page fictional/aggregate logic model and indicator sheet with numerator, denominator, data source, equity measure, limitations and an implementation/exit hypothesis.
An ethics and partnership memo that addresses local leadership, permissions, confidentiality, data stewardship, dissemination, authorship and relevant review.
A short oral presentation with an explicit “what we do not know” and no copied patient images or protected records.
assignment.passingRule: No validated passing threshold; instructor may require revision. This is not official fellowship assessment or board certification.

assessment.rubrics: Use each unit’s stated criterion/rubric; learners should cite sources and uncertainty. Cases are fictional except linked authentic, lawfully viewable case resources; no patient images are copied.
assessment.validityNotice: Locally designed formative course work, not validated board questions or predictor. No passing score is validated.

studyHours.plan: 90 hours of non-video independent work over 12 units (approximately 7.5 hours/unit, including open readings, structured case exercises, peer feedback and capstone). This is an instructional planning estimate, distinct from the 36-hour video floor and not clinical training time.

unitMap.text: Global EM as a field: clinical practice, systems and roles
coveredTopics: Definitions and scope; systems-building; reciprocal partnership; local leadership; limits of short-term visits.

unitMap.text: Emergency-care systems and needs assessment
coveredTopics: WHO ECSF; access and first contact; referral; workforce/coordination; systems assessment; indicators and data quality.

unitMap.text: First-contact acute care in resource-constrained settings
coveredTopics: WHO/ICRC BEC; difficulty breathing, shock, altered mental status, injury; life-course considerations; handover.

unitMap.text: Prehospital care, triage, referral and continuity
coveredTopics: Access, triage, prehospital pathways, transport barriers, referral, handoff, crowding and continuity.

unitMap.text: Humanitarian response, disaster and EMT operations
coveredTopics: All-hazards response; WHO EMT initiative; local authority and coordination; team capability/registration; disaster risk; surge and safe exit.

unitMap.text: Humanitarian law, ethics, protection and conflict health
coveredTopics: International humanitarian law; health care in danger; human rights; safeguarding, consent, confidentiality, staff safety and humanitarian principles.

unitMap.text: Refugee health, displacement and cross-cultural practice
coveredTopics: Refugee/displacement health; culturally responsive communication; interpreter use; gender and disability inclusion; privacy; access and continuity.

unitMap.text: Global public health, outbreaks and emergency surveillance
coveredTopics: Outbreak readiness; surveillance; line list; case definitions; epidemic curves; infection prevention; risk communication; One Health/climate considerations.

unitMap.text: Global EM research, implementation science and grant design
coveredTopics: Research design; measurement; biostatistics; implementation/program evaluation; co-authorship; local leadership; grant logic model.

unitMap.text: Programme design, funding, monitoring and sustainability
coveredTopics: Logic models; stakeholder map; budget assumptions; monitoring and evaluation; health policy; localization; sustainability and exit.

unitMap.text: Teaching, leadership and bidirectional capacity strengthening
coveredTopics: Adult learning; instructor development; mentoring; leadership; supervision; bidirectional learning; evaluation of educational programs.

unitMap.text: Clinical integration, board cognition and professional limits

topicGaps: A full 36 hours of verified, free, public lecture recordings specific to global EM were not confirmed.
No verified runtime ledger for the indexed Global EM Grand Rounds video or otherwise useful BEC videos.
No public BWH full lecture archive or source curriculum was found; proprietary, login-only, paid courses and in-person content are not counted.
